evals.name: full-portfolio-from-real-code
evals.prompt:
Document the Python library at /Users/vbezdek/Work/skillstack/benchmarks/documentation-generator/fixtures/slugify-utils/

First read the source files to understand what the library does (use Bash ls and Read tools). The library has: slugify_utils/core.py, slugify_utils/validators.py, slugify_utils/languages.py, slugify_utils/__init__.py, tests/test_core.py, pyproject.toml, and a minimal README.md.

Then generate the full documentation portfolio for this library. Apply all phases of your documentation workflow — analysis, planning, structuring, writing, and validation. Save every output file to the CURRENT directory (not to the fixture path). Print the list of files you created at the end.
evals.expected_output: Multi-file doc portfolio with explicit audience analysis table, prioritized doc plan with P0/P1/P2 markers, and at least one tutorial file with Before You Begin and What You Will Learn sections.
expectations: A '## Target Audiences' section OR a table explicitly labelled 'Target Audiences' or 'Audiences' exists in at least one output file, containing a markdown table with AT LEAST 2 rows where each row names a distinct user type (e.g. 'Library Consumer', 'Contributor', 'Maintainer', 'Integrator'). A section that only mentions 'developers' generically without distinct rows does NOT satisfy this.

A documentation plan, priority section, or structured doc index exists containing EXPLICIT priority markers — either P0/P1/P2, or must-have/should-have/nice-to-have, or Critical/Important/Optional — applied to at least 3 distinct documents. A flat list of documents without any priority notation does NOT satisfy this. Timing-only guidance like 'Read First: Yes' does NOT satisfy this.

At least one output file contains BOTH a '## Before You Begin' OR '## Prerequisites' section AND a '## What You Will Learn' OR '## Learning Objectives' OR '## By the end of this guide' section. Both sections must appear in the same file. A getting-started file with only prerequisites OR only learning objectives but not both does NOT satisfy this.

evals.name: api-reference-with-error-table
evals.prompt:
Read the Python library at /Users/vbezdek/Work/skillstack/benchmarks/documentation-generator/fixtures/slugify-utils/ and generate its API reference documentation.

Read core.py, validators.py, and languages.py first using Read or Bash tools. Then produce: (1) a complete API reference for all public functions, (2) a quickstart guide for new users, and (3) a troubleshooting guide for common errors. Save all output to the CURRENT directory. Print the list of files at the end.
evals.expected_output: API reference with code sample at top + error table, quickstart with prerequisites section, troubleshooting with symptom/cause/fix table.
expectations: The API reference file contains a working code example (a fenced code block of at least 3 lines) BEFORE the first parameter or function-signature table in the file. A code example that only appears at the end of the file, or after all function documentation, does NOT satisfy this — the sample must come first.

A troubleshooting or error reference section exists containing a table OR structured list that maps at least 3 distinct error conditions to their causes or fixes. The table must have entries covering SlugError or ValueError (the actual exceptions in the codebase). A generic 'if something goes wrong, check your input' paragraph without specific error entries does NOT satisfy this.

The quickstart or getting-started file contains an explicit prerequisite block — either '## Prerequisites', '## Before You Begin', or '## Requirements' — listing at least Python version AND one installation command. A file that jumps straight to usage examples without a named prerequisite section does NOT satisfy this.

evals.name: architecture-and-contributor-docs
evals.prompt:
Read the Python library at /Users/vbezdek/Work/skillstack/benchmarks/documentation-generator/fixtures/slugify-utils/ and produce its architecture and contributor documentation.

Read all source files. Then produce: (1) an architecture decision record (ADR) explaining why language-specific transliteration was separated into languages.py rather than inlined, (2) a contributor guide, and (3) a documentation gap register listing what documentation is still missing. Save all files to the CURRENT directory. Print the list of files at the end.
evals.expected_output: ADR with ## Status, ## Context, ## Decision, ## Consequences headings; CONTRIBUTING.md with setup/workflow/code-style sections; GAPS.md or Known Gaps section listing missing docs.
expectations: At least one file uses Architecture Decision Record format with ALL FOUR of these sections present as ## or ### headings in the same file: 'Status' AND 'Context' AND 'Decision' AND 'Consequences'. A file that has only 2 or 3 of these as headings does NOT satisfy this. The Status section must appear before Context in the file.

A contributor guide or CONTRIBUTING.md file exists that explicitly covers ALL THREE of: (a) development environment setup (install/clone/virtualenv steps), (b) a code style or formatting standard (linting, formatting tool, or naming convention), AND (c) how to submit changes (PR process, branch naming, or commit message format). A CONTRIBUTING.md that covers only 1 or 2 of these does NOT satisfy this.

A gaps register, 'Known Gaps', 'Documentation Gaps', or 'Missing Documentation' section exists in at least one output file. It must contain at least one specific gap item (e.g. a doc type or topic that is not yet covered). The text 'No known gaps' also satisfies this IF it is followed by a date or version. A completely absent gaps section does NOT satisfy this.
